jobs.title: Environmental Specialist I
jobs.description:
Company Description

Veolia in North America is the top-ranked environmental company in the United States for three consecutive years, and the country's largest private water operator and technology provider as well as hazardous waste and pollution treatment leader. It offers a full spectrum of water, waste, and energy management services, including water and wastewater treatment, commercial and hazardous waste collection and disposal, energy consulting and resource recovery. Veolia helps commercial, industrial, healthcare, higher education and municipality customers throughout North America. Headquartered in Boston, Veolia has more than 10,000 employees working at more than 350 locations across North America.

Job Description

Position Purpose:

This position provides specialized transportation and disposal services to our clients. Responsibilities include manifesting, packaging, spill response, labeling, loading/unloading, coordinating transportation, and sampling/profiling material while adhering to state and federal environmental, health, and safety regulations.

Primary Duties /Responsibilities

Sample waste streams according to prescribed policies and procedures.
Manifesting, packaging, spill clean-up response and remedial activities, labeling, loading, off loading, and coordinating transportation.
Maintain a professional image to clients by answering inquiries and suggesting solutions to existing/potential problems.
Comply and enforce all compliance, health, safety, and procedures in accordance with VES-TS policies.
Become familiar with all U. S. Department of Transportation (DOT)/Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and VES-TS regulations required in submitting paperwork to expedite disposal of hazardous waste.
Operate and maintain all equipment in a professional manner to ensure optimum efficiency and effectiveness.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Education / Experience / Background:

High School diploma or General Educational Development (GED) required
Bachelor's degree in Chemistry or a related science discipline preferred

Knowledge / Skills / Abilities

Strong team player
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills
Time management: the ability to organize and manage multiple deadlines
Strong customer service orientation
Computer proficiency
Ability to follow through on assignments.

Required Certification / Licenses / Training

40-hour HAZWOPER Certification
Valid Driver's License
Ability to obtain a Class A or B Commercial Drivers License (CDL) with Hazardous (H) endorsement

Additional Information

Benefits:
Veolia's comprehensive benefits package includes paid time off policies, as well as health, dental, vision, life insurance, savings accounts, tuition reimbursement, paid volunteering and more. In addition, employees are also entitled to participate in an employer sponsored 401(k) plan, to save for retirement.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer! All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status.

Disclaimer: The salary, other compensation, and benefits information is accurate as of the date of this posting. The Company reserves the right to modify this information at any time, subject to applicable law.

jobs.title: WATER QUALITY ANALYST
jobs.description:
OPEN COMPETITIVE RECRUITMENT

Open to all qualified candidates

Tentative Examination Dates For This Recruitment

Week of 10/05/26 - Blind Application & Supplemental scoring

Week of 10/19/26 - Oral examination

Under general supervision, to perform a variety of analytical and technical tasks in the administration of the City’s Water Quality Programs; assist the utility in ensuring regulatory compliance with Federal and State water legislation and policy; and perform related work as required.

Essential Functions

Develops, implements and regularly updates the Water Division’s Water Quality and Production programs and trains employees as necessary; participates as a member of the Water Division’s water regulation compliance group; advises the Production/Operations section staff of water quality concerns that may affect treatment and/or operations; assists with oversight of the Water Division’s Cross Connection Control Program; performs analysis and conducts studies; assists in the preparation of water data reports, plans, procedures, specifications, research and the administration of contracts; responds to customer water quality inquiries and complaints; maintains files and databases; compiles data and daily logs of water production, water quality activities and analyzes and interprets results of water tests; participates in consultations with regulatory agencies such as the State Department of Health, Los Angeles County Department of Health Services, Environmental Protection Agency, Regional Water Quality Control Board and other interested parties; assists in the preparation of the applications for the National Pollution Discharge Elimination System(NPDES) permit program and reviews data for compliance of established permits under NPDES; performs periodic review of cross connection program records to ensure compliance to Title 17 requirements; performs laboratory inspections; reviews and updates a variety of basic laboratory procedures for bacteriological testing and qualitative testing of water samples in the laboratory and in the field; reviews laboratory logs and records for accuracy and prepares various reports; develops and implements the water laboratory quality assurance/quality control procedures and maintains documentation; administers contract laboratory services including scheduling, reporting and invoice processing; reviews and interprets laboratory reports; participates in laboratory accreditation and may act as signatory for laboratory reports; attends conferences and meetings related to regulatory compliance of permits and programs implemented by the Water Division; drives on City business.

Minimum Qualifications

Employment Standards:

Knowledge of principles of water treatment and quality tests; regulatory codes and laws relating to the operation of a water system, including but not limited to Title 17 (cross connection) and Title 22 (water quality); NPDES permit program; occupational hazards and safety precautions in the workplace; Federal and State requirements and standards for analyzing potable water; research methods and analytical techniques; modern office procedures, practices and equipment, including but not limited to computer equipment and supporting software.

Skill in Microsoft Office Windows programs, including but not limited to Access, Excel, and Word.

Ability to work according to safety standards; research, analyze, and interpret water quality or environmental regulations or issues and prepare written reports; compile, review, and analyze data; maintain records and files; read and interpret blueprints and diagrams; perform basic laboratory water testing; operate assigned laboratory equipment; communicate effectively both verbally and in writing; establish and maintain effective working relationships with supervisors, fellow employees, the public, and outside agencies.

Education/Training:
Graduation from high school or equivalent, supplemented by two years of technical training, jobexperience and/or college courses such as biology, chemistry, computer applications, environmental science and othersubjects related to water quality and production and three years of recent experience in water quality analysis, or arelated profession in a public or private water utility system or related industry.

License & Certificates:
A valid T-2 Water Treatment Operator certificate issued by the State of California Department of Health Services and a valid D-2 Water Distribution Operator certificate issued by the State of California Department of Health is required within two years of appointment; certification by AWWA or CWEA as a Water Quality Laboratory Analyst Grade I at time of appointment; a valid California Class “C” Driver’s License or equivalent at time of appointment.

Supplemental Information

None.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Safety Coordinator
jobs.description:
The Environmental, Health, and Safety Coordinator supports EMPWR USA's environmental, health, and safety (EHS) program at the McMinnville food manufacturing facilities. This role provides hands-on support for daily EHS activities, inspections, training, documentation, incident and environmental event response, corrective action follow-up, and employee engagement. The EHS Coordinator works closely with the EHS Manager and partners with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Quality, Sanitation, Warehouse, Human Resources, and site leadership to identify and reduce risk, reinforce safe and environmentally responsible work practices, and support a proactive EHS culture.

Responsibilities

EHS Program Support and Coordination

Support the implementation, administration, and continuous improvement of the site EHS management system, policies, procedures, standards, and work practices.
Serve as a visible floor-level EHS resource for employees and leaders, answering questions, reinforcing expectations, and escalating significant concerns to the EHS Manager.
Partner with department leaders and employees to support EHS expectations in daily operations, projects, change management, and continuous improvement activities.
Assist with EHS inspections, observations, communications, action tracking, and other activities that strengthen accountability for safe and environmentally responsible work practices.

Regulatory Compliance

Support compliance with applicable OSHA, Oregon OSHA, EPA, Oregon Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ), and other relevant federal, state, and local EHS requirements.
Maintain required EHS records, logs, documentation, permits, training records, regulatory postings, and other compliance files in an organized and audit-ready manner.
Assist the EHS Manager with regulatory inspections, customer or third-party EHS audits, documentation requests, permit-related activities, and corrective action responses.
Support updates to site programs, training materials, procedures, and records when regulatory or operational requirements change.

Environmental Compliance and Management Support

Support site environmental programs related to waste management, hazardous materials, air emissions, wastewater, stormwater, spill prevention and response, and other applicable environmental requirements.
Assist with routine environmental inspections, monitoring, sampling coordination, recordkeeping, and reporting activities under the direction of the EHS Manager.
Help ensure hazardous, universal, and other regulated wastes are properly identified, labeled, stored, handled, documented, and prepared for disposal in accordance with established procedures.
Maintain environmental records and documentation such as inspection logs, waste records, manifests, vendor documentation, spill records, and permit-related files.
Support environmental incident and spill response activities, including documentation, corrective action tracking, and replenishment of spill response materials.

Occupational Health, Hazard Identification, and Risk Reduction

Conduct routine workplace inspections, safety observations, job hazard analyses, and other proactive hazard identification activities under the direction of the EHS Manager.
Partner with Operations, Maintenance, Engineering, Sanitation, Warehouse, and other functions to identify hazards and support practical risk reduction measures.
Support critical safety and occupational health programs, including lockout/tagout, machine guarding, powered industrial trucks, hazard communication and chemical safety, personal protective equipment, confined space, fall protection, hot work, ergonomics, hearing conservation, respiratory protection, contractor safety, and emergency response, as applicable.
Document identified hazards, track corrective actions to completion, and follow up with responsible owners to help ensure controls remain effective and sustainable.

Incident Investigation and Corrective Action

Respond to workplace injuries, incidents, near misses, environmental releases, spills, and EHS concerns and promptly notify the EHS Manager and appropriate leaders of significant events.
Support investigations by gathering facts, photographs, witness information, documentation, and other relevant evidence, and participate in root-cause analysis as assigned.
Assist with injury, incident, and environmental event documentation, corrective and preventive action tracking, and coordination with Human Resources and operational leaders as appropriate.
Maintain accurate EHS incident files and help identify recurring issues or trends that may require additional corrective action or program improvement.

Training and EHS Culture

Coordinate and deliver new-hire EHS orientation and assigned recurring EHS training for employees, contractors, and visitors.
Maintain accurate training records and assist with scheduling required refresher, department-specific, or compliance training.
Support leaders with safety talks, employee coaching, EHS communications, signage, and timely correction of unsafe conditions, behaviors, or environmental concerns.
Promote employee participation in hazard reporting, near-miss reporting, environmental concern reporting, safety observations, and continuous improvement efforts.
Support the site Safety Committee and other EHS engagement activities by coordinating meetings, preparing materials, documenting minutes, and tracking action items.

Emergency Preparedness and Response

Support emergency action and response programs, drills, inspections, response planning, spill response readiness, and follow-up activities.
Assist with maintaining emergency and spill response equipment, supplies, contact information, and related documentation.
Provide support during workplace emergencies, environmental releases, and other EHS events consistent with training and assigned responsibilities.

EHS Data, Reporting, and Continuous Improvement

Maintain EHS databases, logs, action trackers, inspection records, training records, environmental records, and other systems used to monitor EHS performance and compliance.
Compile EHS metrics, incident information, environmental data, audit findings, training completion data, and corrective action status for review by the EHS Manager and site leadership.
Use observations and available data to identify recurring issues, recommend improvements, and support site EHS initiatives and continuous improvement efforts.

Job Requirements

Associate's or bachelor's degree in environmental health and safety, occupational safety, environmental science, or a related field preferred; equivalent education and relevant experience will be considered.
Minimum of 2 years of environmental, health, and safety experience, preferably in a manufacturing environment; food manufacturing experience is a plus.
Experience conducting workplace inspections, supporting EHS training, maintaining compliance documentation, and participating in incident investigations is preferred.
Working knowledge of OSHA requirements and general manufacturing safety practices; familiarity with environmental compliance requirements and Oregon OSHA or Oregon DEQ experience is preferred.
Familiarity with manufacturing safety programs such as lockout/tagout, machine guarding, powered industrial trucks, chemical safety, PPE, confined space, fall protection, industrial hygiene, and contractor safety.
Experience supporting environmental programs such as hazardous or universal waste, stormwater, wastewater, air emissions, spill prevention and response, or environmental recordkeeping is preferred.
Demonstrated ability to build positive working relationships, communicate EHS expectations effectively, and work collaboratively with employees and leaders at all levels.
Strong written, verbal, facilitation, and training skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and professionally.
Strong organizational and problem-solving skills with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple priorities and follow corrective actions through completion.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and the ability to learn and use EHS, training, reporting, and compliance management systems.
OSHA 30-Hour training and First Aid/CPR/AED certification are preferred; environmental or hazardous materials training is a plus, and the ability to obtain required training or certifications after hire is expected.
Ability to work in an active manufacturing environment, spend significant time on the production floor, use required PPE, and provide occasional support outside normal business hours when operational, training, or emergency needs require.
